description: Out-of-tree explicit spec for the slice-length defect of nim-libp2p's BytesView.toOpenArray. The template body (libp2p/utils/bytesview.nim:18-19) `v.data.toOpenArray(v.rpos + b, v.rpos + e - b)` yields length e-2b+1 — exactly b elements short of the inclusive view-relative law e-b+1 (Nim system toOpenArray semantics — official example s.toOpenArray(1,3) == [1,2,3], 3 elements) — and coinciding with a half-open law e-b only at b=1 (where the template's inclusive interval is mis-derived by subtracting the start offset twice). Two CONSTRUCTED-IR carriers (the subject is a template, not a materializable func): bvSliceLenActual (defect — b pinned at 1, model e-1, adopted law result == e; every e in the domain is a counterexample) and bvSliceLenControl (control — b pinned at 0, model e+1, law result == e+1; solver-level injection guard). The adopted LAW is DATA, not engine prose: canonicalSpecIR names one law symbol per carrier (bvSliceLenLaw1, bvSliceLenLaw0) and states its body, so the obligation (model == law) is fully determined by this document and the engine hardcodes no law content. A confirmed counterexample is replayed against the ORIGINAL template through a stamped harness observing len(bv.toOpenArray(1, e)) on BytesView.init(@[byte 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]) — the observation, not the model, decides. The subject tree is READ-ONLY (Zero-Footprint).

carriers.name: bvSliceLenActual
carriers.grounding: bytesview.nim:18-19 — the template's actual index arithmetic with b pinned at 1: underlying inclusive range [rpos+1, rpos+e-1], length = e - 2*1 + 1 = e - 1; machine-extracted model, not a carried body (the subject is a template)

carriers.name: bvSliceLenControl
carriers.grounding: at b=0 the actual length is e+1, equal to the inclusive law e-0+1 — the b=0 path exercised by the production call sites (noise.nim:314,333: 32-byte destinations) and by the sibling `data` template's inclusive idiom (bytesview.nim:21-22); injection guard only

semanticCaveats: toOpenArray is a template — the carriers are CONSTRUCTED IR; the solver verifies the ADOPTED MODEL, and the subject connection is the stamped replay harness, which imports libp2p/utils/bytesview and expands the template from the defining module (Nim manual: template symbols are bound from the definition scope)

the adopted law is stated as DATA in canonicalSpecIR (bvSliceLenLaw1 = e at b = 1, bvSliceLenLaw0 = e + 1 at b = 0) — the engine parses the named definitions and hardcodes no law content; the two carriers' obligations are the model-equals-law equalities over the SAME domain variable
the domain 1 <= e <= 5 is bound to the replay fixture BytesView.init(@[byte 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]) with rpos = 0 (a view-relative inclusive [1..e] is valid up to e = 5)
each carrier has exactly ONE model parameter (e); b is fixed at 1 (defect) / 0 (control) — a deliberate narrowing required by the single-parameter replay contract
the defect claim (e - 1) == e is violated for EVERY e in the domain — the solver selects one witness; the replay observes that pinned instance on the subject's actual bytes
the replay observation is the integer length echoed between the AXIOM_REPLAY_BEGIN/AXIOM_REPLAY_END markers
subject pins use the module file's content sha256; git object IDs (a SHA-1 repo) are a different hash kind and are recorded separately in the run evidence
